`field_specs` must be a list of dictionaries in declaration order. Every specification must contain a unique non-empty string `name`, a `kind` equal to `"text"`, `"integer"`, or `"labels"`, and may contain a Boolean `required` flag, defaulting to `False`. No other keys are allowed. Malformed specifications must raise `ValueError`.

`raw_values` must be a mapping; otherwise raise `TypeError`. Return `(record, errors)`, where both values are new dictionaries. Process fields in specification order:

- `text` accepts only strings. Strip surrounding whitespace. A required text value that becomes empty produces `"required"`.
- `integer` accepts integers but not Booleans.
- `labels` accepts only a list of strings and preserves its order and duplicates. The returned list must be a fresh copy.
- A supplied value of the wrong type produces `"invalid type"` and is omitted from `record`.

Unknown input names must be reported as a sorted list under `errors["__extra__"]`. Inputs and nested lists must never be mutated, and no mutable value in the result may alias an input value.

import unittest
from collections import UserDict

from solution import compile_record


class CompileRecordTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_normal_conversion_order_extras_and_no_aliasing(self):
        labels = ["red", "red", "blue"]
        raw = {"age": 7, "tags": labels, "title": "  Hello  ", "z": 1, "a": 2}
        specs = [
            {"name": "title", "kind": "text", "required": True},
            {"name": "age", "kind": "integer"},
            {"name": "tags", "kind": "labels"},
        ]
        specs_before = [dict(item) for item in specs]
        raw_before = {**raw, "tags": list(labels)}
        record, errors = compile_record(specs, raw)
        self.assertEqual(record, {"title": "Hello", "age": 7, "tags": ["red", "red", "blue"]})
        self.assertEqual(list(record), ["title", "age", "tags"])
        self.assertEqual(errors, {"__extra__": ["a", "z"]})
        self.assertIsNot(record["tags"], labels)
        record["tags"].append("new")
        self.assertEqual(labels, ["red", "red", "blue"])
        self.assertEqual(specs, specs_before)
        self.assertEqual(raw, raw_before)

    def test_missing_empty_and_wrong_types(self):
        specs = [
            {"name": "required_missing", "kind": "integer", "required": True},
            {"name": "optional_missing", "kind": "text"},
            {"name": "blank", "kind": "text", "required": True},
            {"name": "count", "kind": "integer"},
            {"name": "labels", "kind": "labels"},
            {"name": "bad_labels", "kind": "labels"},
        ]
        record, errors = compile_record(specs, {
            "blank": " \t ", "count": True, "labels": [], "bad_labels": ["ok", 3]
        })
        self.assertEqual(record, {"labels": []})
        self.assertEqual(errors, {
            "required_missing": "required", "blank": "required",
            "count": "invalid type", "bad_labels": "invalid type"
        })

    def test_optional_empty_text_is_retained(self):
        record, errors = compile_record([{"name": "x", "kind": "text"}], {"x": "   "})
        self.assertEqual(record, {"x": ""})
        self.assertEqual(errors, {})

    def test_mapping_subclass_and_empty_specs(self):
        self.assertEqual(compile_record([], UserDict({"x": 1})), ({}, {"__extra__": ["x"]}))

    def test_raw_values_must_be_mapping(self):
        for value in (None, [], [("x", 1)], "x"):
            with self.subTest(value=value), self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                compile_record([], value)

    def test_malformed_specifications(self):
        invalid = [
            None, {}, {"name": "", "kind": "text"}, {"name": 1, "kind": "text"},
            {"name": "x"}, {"name": "x", "kind": "float"},
            {"name": "x", "kind": "text", "required": 1},
            {"name": "x", "kind": "text", "extra": False},
        ]
        for spec in invalid:
            with self.subTest(spec=spec), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                compile_record([spec], {})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            compile_record("not a list", {})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            compile_record([{"name": "x", "kind": "text"}, {"name": "x", "kind": "integer"}], {})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
